vault.boundary: Shared, not private: every Bot in this workspace may use these entries. A password filled into the shared browser, and the session it opens, can be read by code running in this workspace, another Bot's included. The Vault keeps values out of chats, transcripts and screenshots; it does not hide them from the workspace. Keep production credentials in a separate, locked workspace, never in one that browses untrusted sites (ADR-0045).
vault.confirmDelete: Delete the Vault entry {name}? Bots can no longer use it. This does not sign the shared browser out or revoke the credential at the service.
vault.create.originNote: The exact https origin the credential belongs to. A fill happens only on a page of that origin, and a sign-in frame or single sign-on on another origin needs its own entry.
vault.create.title: Add a credential
vault.deleteNote: Deleting stops new uses at once. It does not sign the browser out, revoke the credential at the service, or erase encrypted backups.
vault.field.name: Name
vault.filledNote: A use records only what happened: “filled” means the fields were filled, not that the sign-in succeeded. One-time codes, passkeys and CAPTCHAs still need a person to take over the browser.
vault.intro: Credentials this workspace's Bots use through references. A Bot sees names and origins; a tool fills the password into the shared browser or adds the token to one fixed request, after an approval. No Bot can read a saved value back, and this page never shows one.
vault.mode.approveAll: This workspace is in Approve all mode: every credential use is allowed without asking anyone and recorded as decided by mode:approve_all. The exact-origin and revision checks still apply.
vault.mode.automatic: Each credential use asks a person: the automatic reviewer never decides one.
vault.mode.manual: Each credential use is asked in the requesting Bot's chat, where its members decide.
vault.replaceNote: The new value replaces the stored one and starts a new revision; earlier approvals and Always answers no longer apply.
vault.requests.none: No request definitions: this token cannot be used until one is added.
vault.requests.note: A Bot can only run these definitions: the method, route and header are fixed here, and it supplies the listed parameters. Every use asks for approval; a request marked may change data is never repeated after an unknown outcome.
vault.requests.params: Parameters, one per line: name path|query|body string|integer|number|boolean [required]
vault.requests.title: Request definitions
vault.sharedNote: Shared with every Bot in this workspace.
vault.summary: Saved logins and tokens for this workspace.
vault.title: Vault
vault.unavailable: The Vault is not available on this server, so credentials cannot be stored or used. Ask the person who runs Deskmates to enable it.
vault.unusable.no_request_definition: not usable: no request definition yet
vault.unusable.vault_unavailable: not usable: the Vault is unavailable
